# spectral.dispersion { #clerq.spectral.dispersion }

```python
spectral.dispersion(mb_solve, field_idx, z_idx=-1, *, window=None)
```

Field dispersion in the frequency domain.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type              | Description                                             | Default    |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| mb_solve  | PropagationSolver | A PropagationSolver object.                             | _required_ |
| field_idx | int               | Field to return spectrum of.                            | _required_ |
| z_idx     | int               | z step at which to return absorption.                   | `-1`       |
| window    | str \| None       | Optional SciPy window name passed to :func:`rabi_freq`. | `None`     |

## Note {.doc-section .doc-section-note}

In the linear regime this is the real part of the linear
susceptibility.

See TP Ogden Thesis Eqn (2.59)
